name: Dimethyltrienolone (Dimethyltren / RU-2420)
lead: Dimethyltrienolone, developmental code RU-2420 and also written 7α,17α-dimethyltrenbolone, is a synthetic, orally active anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS). It is a 17α-alkylated derivative of the 19-nortestosterone family that includes nandrolone, trenbolone and metribolone [1][2].

It was first described in 1967 and has never been marketed for medical use [1]. Reference works describe it as an extremely potent agonist of the androgen and progesterone receptors, with animal bioassays reporting more than 100 times the anabolic and androgenic potency of methyltestosterone [1][2]. It has been called "perhaps the most potent" AAS developed, a characterisation that Wikipedia attributes to a secondary source rather than to human data [1].

No human clinical, pharmacokinetic or safety studies have been published. Its liver toxicity is described as likely to be severe on structural grounds, but this too is inferred from related compounds rather than measured in people [1][2]. It circulates in bodybuilding circles only as an unapproved research chemical.

paras: Dimethyltrienolone is described as an androgen receptor agonist that also activates the progesterone receptor, so it is both an AAS and a progestogen [1]. Wikipedia lists binding affinities of about 180% (androgen receptor) and 306% (progesterone receptor) relative to testosterone in a comparison table [1].

Like trenbolone, it is not a substrate for 5α-reductase or aromatase, so it is not converted into more potent androgens in tissues such as prostate or skin and has no estrogenic activity [1][2]. Its 17α-methyl group (oral activity) and 7α-methyl group (resistance to metabolism) are described as contributing to resistance to hepatic breakdown and as being likely to make it markedly hepatotoxic [1][2]. Human pharmacokinetic data are unavailable [2].

It is a derivative of trenbolone carrying methyl groups at the 7α and 17α positions, with the triene (4,9,11) unsaturation of the trenbolone family [2]. The reported formula is C20H26O2 with a molar mass of about 298.4 g/mol [2].

The compound was developed under the "RU" code series of Roussel Uclaf, a French pharmaceutical company, and described in 1967 during structure-activity work on nortestosterone derivatives. It was never developed as a drug [1][2].

Dimethyltrienolone has no approved status in any jurisdiction and is sold, where it appears, as a research chemical [2]. Wikipedia notes that much of what is said about its potency comes from animal bioassays, receptor-binding studies and a popular book on steroids rather than from clinical work [1].
No studies found. Only animal bioassays and receptor-binding experiments of the compound have been reported [1][2].

timeline.event: Dimethyltrienolone (RU-2420) first described in the literature; never marketed [1].

card.summary: An obscure, never-marketed trenbolone analog with reported animal potency far above methyltestosterone and no human data.
card.note: No human studies exist; described as likely severely hepatotoxic. Not approved anywhere.

quick.overview:
Dimethyltrienolone is an experimental oral anabolic steroid made in the 1960s by Roussel Uclaf. It was never sold as a medicine and has not been tested in people.

In animal assays it was reported as extremely potent, and some commentators call it one of the strongest steroids ever made. All of that rests on rodent and receptor-binding work.
quick.mechanism: It activates the androgen and progesterone receptors strongly and, like trenbolone, is not converted by aromatase or 5α-reductase. Methyl groups at two positions make it resistant to liver breakdown, allowing oral activity.
quick.risks: No human safety data exist. Reference sources describe it as expected to be highly liver-toxic and note progestogenic effects. It has no approved medical use and is available only as an unregulated research chemical.
